daniels-county: Daniels County is home to roughly 1,600 people, 11% of whom live in poverty, according to U.S. census data. County Commissioner Tammi Fladager said the Bridger Pipeline could provide financial opportunity.
valley-county-commission: Valley County would receive annual tax revenue from the Bridger Pipeline, which could help the county repair roads and bridges or invest in other community services.
kleeman: Kent Kleeman runs cattle and raises pigs just up the road from Jerry Arnold's farm. Kleeman says money from the pipeline easement would help him and his wife, Kim, pay down their debt on the ranch.
thielen: Bob and Missy Thielen's ranch is just outside Baker. Bob Thielen said he trusts the company. He also has questions about the pipeline. “What is the benefit to the American people?” he asked.
jerry-arnold: Jerry Arnold farms grain near the U.S.-Canada border in Montana. He hopes the Bridger Pipeline will bring some financial relief to his farm.
carter-county-commission: Carter County commissioners say existing pipeline infrastructure accounts for the vast majority of the county’s property tax revenue.
mike-kjos: Mike Kjos farms northwest of Fairview, where pipelines already run through his property. He wants landowners to be treated fairly during negotiations with Bridger.
fort-peck-tribes: The Bridger Pipeline's preferred route skirts the Fort Peck Reservation to the north, coming within two miles of the reservation's boundary at its closest point. Tribal leaders say a spill could put thousands of people’s drinking water at risk.
fladager: Daniels County Commissioner Tammi Fladager said a project like the Bridger Pipeline would provide a much-needed economic boon for eastern Montana.
